findings.rule: A configured command must actually be executed by the entrypoints that claim to run it
findings.trigger: The pinned CLI dispatches its builtin generate-check case before the configured command (cmd/ledger-tool/main.go:141, reached both from the top level and from @ledger-tool steps at internal/governance/runner.go:72-77), so governance.json's generate-check steps are dead. Reproduced in a /tmp scratch copy whose configured generate-check body was replaced with 'sh -c echo CONFIGURED-BODY-RAN': 'go run ./tool/bootstrap.go generate-check --output lib/l10n/generated -- sh -c echo BUILTIN-BODY-RAN' printed BUILTIN-BODY-RAN and exited 0, never running the configured body. The new recipe (justfile:87) and the check step therefore repeat the same '--output lib/l10n/generated -- flutter gen-l10n' argv a third time without ever executing the configured command (the CLI already prefers a configured command of the same name for doctor at cmd/ledger-tool/main.go:88-91)
findings.impact: The configured command is unreachable configuration: editing it (output path, flags, timeout) changes nothing, while recipes-check still counts it as reachable through the check step's @ledger-tool delegation. The policy file that reviewers read and the argv that actually runs can drift apart silently; today the duplication is behaviourally harmless only because the check step's argv happens to be identical
findings.recommendation: Keep one authoritative declaration: either delete the shadowed configured command so the builtin plus the recipe own the argv, or extend the doctor-style preference so a configured command of the same name wins over the builtin, then re-export and re-pin the bundle; document that a recipe cannot invoke a configured command whose name collides with a builtin

findings.rule: Every gate step a workflow runs directly must be reproducible from a documented recipe
findings.trigger: The 'Verify committed generated files and lockfile' step runs 'git diff --exit-code -- pubspec.lock lib/l10n/generated' and the iOS job runs raw 'xcrun simctl shutdown|delete Ledger-CI' (lines 115 and 118); recipes-check only inspects bootstrap.go, cmd/ledger-tool and @ledger-tool invocations (internal/governance/recipes.go:25-29) and a --root-prefixed bootstrap invocation escapes the same way, so these steps are invisible and no recipe reaches them while recipes-check exits 0
findings.impact: The pinned agreement check cannot see gate steps that live only in the workflow, so a future CI-only assertion can be added without any developer-reproducible entrypoint while the gate keeps reporting that workflows, justfile and policy agree. The substance of the generated-file and lockfile assertion is reproducible today through just check (generate-check) and just bootstrap (--enforce-lockfile), so this is a coverage and documentation gap rather than a broken gate
findings.recommendation: Add a configured command/recipe for the committed-generated-file and lockfile assertion, or have the producer flag unrecognised direct workflow invocations and re-pin; until then state in docs/governance.md that recipes-check covers commands invoked through the pinned entrypoints only
